TextWidget.Text: Material Swap Tool (F8)
Opens or closes the Documentation window, which covers every tool in the toolkit.
Sets the scope of Preview, Dry Run, Apply and Check LOD Mismatches to the entities selected in the editor. Changes nothing in the scene; the status line shows how many are in scope.
Sets the scope to every entity in the scene whose name or prefab name contains the text in the box below. Type the text first; an empty box matches nothing. Changes nothing by itself.
Whole Scene
Sets the scope to every entity in the open scene. Changes nothing by itself; Apply asks for confirmation when more than 50 entities are in scope.
Continuous Recolor
Opens the Continuous Recolor panel, which tints whatever you select by material category for as long as it is armed.
Mesh Blend
Opens the Mesh Blend panel: checks why the terrain color is not blending onto the base of the selected entity, and tunes the blend height, softness and noise. Opening it changes nothing.
Text used by Filtered mode (matched against entity and prefab names) and by Select by Material (matched against material names). Partial text works and case is ignored.
Rules (from material -> to material -> color factor, optional). To material can be weighted: matA:4, matB:1
Optional color factor set where this rule swaps a material, as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA. Leave empty to leave the color alone.
Swaps the From and To materials of this rule only. Edits the rules list, not the scene; click again to swap back.
Removes this rule from the list. No confirmation and no undo; the scene and saved presets are not affected.
+ Add Rule
Adds an empty rule row at the end of the rules list.
Get Input Rules from Selection
Adds one rule per material found on the entities selected in the editor, with From filled in and To left blank. Materials that already have a rule are skipped. The scene is not changed.
Delete Blanks
Removes every rule whose To material is empty, including rows that only have a From material. No confirmation and no undo for the rules list; the scene is not changed.
Select Rule Matches in Editor
Selects in the editor every entity in the whole scene that uses any From material in the rules list, whatever the scope mode. Replaces the editor selection; changes no materials.
Select by Material (filter box)
Selects in the editor every entity in the whole scene that uses a material whose name contains the text in the filter box. Replaces the editor selection; changes no materials.
Fill Rules From Entity (blank rules only)

Fills the empty To side of existing rules by searching the selected prefab for parts with the same name and tags that already carry a different material. Never adds rows or overwrites a To. The scene is not changed.
Clear All Rules
Removes every rule from the list after asking for confirmation. The rules list has no undo; presets saved on disk and the scene are not affected.
Clear All Input (FROM)
Blanks the From material on every rule and keeps the rows and their To materials. Asks first; the rules list has no undo.
Clear All Output (TO)
Blanks the To material on every rule and keeps the rows and their From materials, ready for Fill Rules From Entity or a Merge-mode preset load. Asks first; the rules list has no undo.
Keeps the rows; blanks one column.
Invert Rules
Swaps From and To on every rule in the list, reversing the direction of the whole rule set. Edits the list only, not the scene; click again to swap back.
Dedupe (Rows)
Keeps the first rule for each From material and deletes every later rule with the same From. No confirmation and no undo for the rules list.
Dedupe (Multi-Output)
Reduces each weighted To entry (matA:4, matB:1) to its first material only. No rows are added or removed. No confirmation and no undo for the rules list.
Infer Rules From An Input Entity (A)
Set Input Entity (A)

Stores the one entity selected in the editor as input entity A for the Infer and Apply buttons in this section. Exactly one entity must be selected. A is kept until you set another or close the panel.
Infer Material from A (Matching Prefab)

Compares A slot by slot with the one entity selected now (B, a copy of the same prefab) and adds rules from each material on A to the material B has there. Materials that already have a rule are skipped. Scene unchanged until Apply.
Infer Color from A (Matching Material)

Reads the color of each tinted material on A and adds one rule per material that keeps the material and sets that color. Needs no second entity. Materials that already have a rule are skipped. Scene unchanged until Apply.
Apply B's Materials to A (Slot-Exact)

Sets each mesh slot on A and its children to the material the selected entity B has in the same slot. Changes the scene directly: asks first, takes a backup, and is logged in Batch History so it can be undone.
On: Apply adds the tag MST_Changed to every entity it changes, so you can find them later by searching that tag. Off: no tag is added.
On: Apply appends _mst to the name of every entity it changes. Off: entity names are left alone.
On: Apply stores a unique ID tag on each entity it changes, so undo finds the right entity even after it is moved or renamed. Off: undo matches entities by name and position.
Entity-wide color factor:

Puts #FFFFFFFF (no tint) in the box. Nothing changes in the scene until Apply, which then resets the entity-wide tint on every entity in scope. To leave entity-wide color alone, empty the box instead.
applies to ALL selected entities, e.g. #38FF92 - Clear resets to no tint
Preset name used by Save Preset and Load Preset. Choosing a preset in Browse Presets fills this in.
Optional comma-separated tags stored with the preset by Save Preset and used for filtering in Browse Presets. Culture tags are detected from the From materials and added automatically.
Save Preset
Saves the rules list to disk as a personal preset under the name in the Name box. An existing preset with that name is overwritten without asking; its old version is kept in the preset History.
Load Preset
Replaces the whole rules list with the preset named in the Name box. No confirmation and no undo for the rules list. A personal preset wins over a built-in one with the same name.
Browse Presets
Opens the preset browser, where you can search the saved presets and load one in Overwrite, Add or Merge mode, optionally inverted.
Opens a list of the entities the rules would change, with world positions and Go buttons. Changes no materials. In Filtered and Whole Scene modes it also selects those entities in the editor.
Dry Run
Runs the rules against the current scope without changing anything and reports the counts in the status line. In Filtered and Whole Scene modes it also selects the affected entities in the editor.

Applies the rules and the entity-wide color to every entity in scope. Takes a backup first, asks before a batch of more than 50 entities or unknown material names, and is logged in Batch History so it can be undone.
Undo Last Batch
Reverts the most recent logged batch for the open scene (the newest Batch History row). No confirmation. Entities it cannot match with confidence are left alone and listed in tool.log.
Dump Slots
Diagnostic. Writes the mesh slots, materials, LOD masks and colors of the selected entities to tool.log (search for [SlotDump]). Changes nothing.
Batch History
Opens Batch History: the logged change batches for this scene, each with its own Undo, Redo and screenshot buttons.
Check LOD Mismatches
Scans the entities in scope for LOD5 mesh slots whose material or color differs from the matching full-detail slot and lists them in a window. Changes nothing.
Revert to Normal

Resets materials and color tints on the entities selected in the editor to their native defaults, however they were changed. Ignores the scope mode. Asks first, takes a backup, and is logged in Batch History.
Fix Color Mismatches
Sets the color of each mismatched LOD5 slot in scope to match its full-detail slot. Runs the check itself if no list is pending. Asks first, takes a backup, and is logged in Batch History.
Fix Material Mismatches

Sets the material of each mismatched LOD5 slot in scope to match its full-detail slot. A different LOD material can be intentional, so review the list first. Asks first, takes a backup, and is logged in Batch History.
Simplify for Export

Whole scene: removes the tracking UID tags this tool added and switches their history to position-based matching. Asks first. It cannot be reversed and undo is less exact afterwards, so use it when you are done iterating.
Backup Scene
Starts a backup of the scene files saved on disk into the backup folder. Unsaved editor changes are not included. The Backup panel (F9) shows the verified result.
Open Backups
Opens the backup folder in Explorer and shows the latest backup in the status line.
